<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAutomationRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da6393f41b2bd2685d2e6b118d78a6c359fb4186` — the merge of head `e5468471255dc453372de98294c1298ec00d0069` into base `183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da6393f41b2bd2685d2e6b118d78a6c359fb4186 && git checkout da6393f41b2bd2685d2e6b118d78a6c359fb4186
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32 e5468471255dc453372de98294c1298ec00d0069 && git checkout -B drift-repro 183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32 && git merge --no-ff e5468471255dc453372de98294c1298ec00d0069

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 183a89e34b8fe29c994d9d5e4865769a1b0bfe32` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — FAIL (L1; this head is not landable)

Head-sha: `62fe62378cc0b8367007587b3dfd6e7b173d5eed`
Reviewer: review-c · read 2026-11-16T07:58Z · first round, L1 only; claim 6910311824
Implemented-by: `claude/area-A5b-34145` · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

**The L2 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is not on this head.** The review tier was unavailable for both runs, so no record was posted. On the seat's ruling, this L1 goes first so the fix can start. The L2 record will be written on the fixed head once the tier is back.

**What holds:** the direction. The four write doors now ask the engine's durable key rule rather than the served read, which makes ADR-0150 D3's refusal real at the write doors. Neither half of the change hands a caller a body or a credential it could not read before.

**Owed:**
1. **F1: the declared narrowing is pinned nowhere.** The `!`, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and R2 all rest on one row. A package-less `PUT /automation/NAME` or `POST /automation` onto a name two packages hold, after the disabled co-holder's slot was withdrawn, in a composition with no metadata store, now answers `409` where it answered `200`.
   - The new runtime file has no shared-name `PUT` or `POST /` case. Its shared-name cases are clone and `DELETE` only, and every rig supplies `saveMetaItem`, so the no-store composition is never built.
   - The engine-side pin went into the disabled-sole-holder case. The `[#33893]` withdrawn-slot block gained no `getHeldFlow` assertion.
   - **Fix:** add one `getHeldFlow` assertion in the withdrawn-slot case, and one no-store rig driving `PUT` and `POST /` onto the shared name.
2. **F2: the BREAKING remedy cannot be applied where the banner says it bites.** The banner is scoped to a composition with no metadata store, but its remedy is the metadata door with `?package=`, which needs one. The addressed write doors deliberately keep their own `409`.
   - **Fix:** name a remedy that exists there (for example, uninstalling the co-holder folds the name back), and say plainly that otherwise the write is refused there exactly as while both holders are enabled.
3. **F3: one release would publish two contradictory accounts.** `.changeset/33905-disabled-sole-holder-flow.md` (from #34048, still pending on `main`) has a BREAKING block, "Three HTTP write doors ask `getFlow` whether the name is held". It says the clone door lets the copy through, the put-back withdraws the name, a `PUT` drops the stored credential and `DELETE` answers `404`. This PR reverses all four before either entry ships.
   - **Fix:** correct the #33905 changeset in this PR. Both entries are pending, so it is a prose face of this release.

**Nit:** the shape of the clone door's shared-name refusal changes from a returned answer to a thrown one, with the same status and code. Either state it, or catch the refusal into the door's own path.

**Checks:** 55 check-runs, 37 success and 18 skipped, none red.

Not governed: the area lands this PR once L1 and the L2 record both read clean.

"Judge a flow name over every holder" therefore does NOT agree with how holders are counted at the bare read and save doors; seat ruling 6884403301 amendment 7, as the engine cites it, keys slots, run keys and bindings over every holder and leaves the doors on the served set (amendment 9). The every-holder read is right for the disabled SOLE holder (the card's stated case) and is the over-reach for a shared name. It does make one thing consistent: the write is already refused while the disabled slot is still held, so `main` answers the same request differently before and after the re-sync. Which way to close that is a ruling, and it has not been made on true facts. The head throws the engine refusal instead ("the caller names no package ... address it by its package"), a remedy a clone caller cannot follow, and the clone body's `package` key (the landing package) invites exactly the wrong reading. Catch the shared-name refusal at the probe and answer name-taken; that also covers the both-enabled case, which already threw on `main`.

S3 (should-fix) — the two pending changesets contradict each other (②). Correct the #33905 entry in this PR.

S4 (should-fix) — R1 and R2 are cited but not on the card, and the claim of record says `Clause-②: no` (③). Post the rulings and amend the claim.

N1 (nit) — `getHeldFlow` is a read that can re-key a slot (`settleFlowName`), as `getFlow` does; its docblock could say so.
